summary: A procedural overview of the steps and filings involved in converting a registered partnership firm into a Limited Liability Partnership.
content:
### Reason for Conversion
A registered partnership firm may be converted into a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, subject to consent of all partners and compliance with prescribed procedural requirements.

### General Procedure
1. Obtaining Digital Signature Certificates (DSC) and Designated Partner Identification Numbers (DPIN) for all partners, where not already held.
2. Filing an application for name reservation with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
3. Filing incorporation documents for the LLP, along with a statement of consent from existing partners.
4. Filing Form 17 to give effect to the conversion, along with a statement of assets and liabilities of the erstwhile firm.

### Post-Conversion Requirements
Following conversion, the LLP is required to update its PAN, bank accounts, GST registration, and other statutory registrations to reflect the new entity, and to comply with LLP-specific annual filing requirements thereafter.
